svg.title: A bounded Borel section on every free orbit, in the original real time
svg.desc: Five vertically arranged panels illustrate the argument in Dense roof groups, two ceilings and eigenfunctions, Section 3A. Lemma 3A.1: the coordinates f_i of a Borel injection separate points. Smoothing h_i(v)=f_i(T_v x) with phi_n produces F_{i,n}(T_s x)=integral phi_n(v-s)h_i(v) dv, whose derivative is G_{i,n}; at least one smooth detector is nonconstant on each free orbit. Rational time translates and a sign give G_F(x)>0 at every x. The binary strip and smooth curve are schematic, not a computed convolution. Lemma 3A.2: for positive rational c and epsilon with epsilon<r/2, a rational level q and derivative G_F at least c throughout the closed time window [-2 epsilon,2 epsilon] define a Borel piece. Starting from a point in that piece, the level difference is positive for 0<s<=2 epsilon and negative for -2 epsilon<=s<0, so distinct points of a piece are separated by strictly more than 2 epsilon. For density, positivity on [-4 epsilon,4 epsilon] and a rational level between the values at -epsilon and epsilon give y=T_s x with |s|<epsilon; then |s+t|<3 epsilon for |t|<=2 epsilon. The countable union D is within time distance strictly less than r/2 of every orbit point. Lemma 3A.3 and Theorem 3A.4: at stage n remove points of S_n within distance strictly less than r of earlier selected points, and join the remaining distinct orbit points when their time distance is strictly less than r. Separation in S_n makes the neighbor sets finite. Least distinguishing binary prefixes give a countable Borel proper coloring; greedy color-by-color selection yields a Borel maximal independent set I_n. The three-node path is an abstract local graph schematic, not an orbit-time scale. Its nonadjacent endpoints share a color and are selected together; its middle vertex is rejected later. Thus C, the union of all I_n, is r-separated, and every point of D is within distance strictly less than r of C. Theorem 3A.4, equation (3A.8): the triangle inequality makes every orbit point strictly less than 3r/2 from C. An orbit's section times are bi-infinite and discrete. If a consecutive gap had length L at least 3r, its midpoint would be at distance at least L/2 at least 3r/2 from every section point, a contradiction. Every consecutive gap lies in [r,3r). The displayed finite schematic section window uses r=1 and precisely the section times 0, 1.5 and 3.5; its gaps are 1.5 and 2. The midpoint of the second gap is 2.5, at distance 1 from each endpoint. These are example returns only, not two prescribed roof values. Theorem 3A.4, equation (3A.9), and Corollary 3A.5: finite intermediate witnesses give the Borel successor S, and rho(c)=tau(c,Sc) lies in [r,3r). The half-open suspension domain is the set of (c,u) with c in C and 0<=u<rho(c). The map Psi(c,u)=T_u c is a Borel bijection with Borel inverse, preserves the original real time, and satisfies T_{rho(c)}c=Sc. The sample columns have roofs 1.5 and 2, with their top endpoints excluded and their bottom endpoints included; the excluded first top is identified with the next base. These diagrams illustrate the proof on every free orbit and discard no orbit.
svg.metadata: Reproducible source: this native SVG. Mathematical source: Dense roof groups, two ceilings and eigenfunctions, Section 3A; Lemmas 3A.1–3A.3, Theorem 3A.4 and Corollary 3A.5. All plotted curves and the local graph are explicitly schematic. The finite schematic section window is exact at r=1.
